newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start with softer tone, track bonds.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start with softer tone, track bonds.

text.p: French shares started on Monday with modest losses, shadowing a downward drift in bond markets, as dealers sat out the eve of the U.S. presidential election, traders said.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 4.58 points or 0.21 percent at 2,135.93 at 0835 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,139 from 2,142 on Thursday's close. The market was closed on Friday for a religious holiday.

Business conglomerate Lagardere loses 2.97 percent after chairman Jean-Luc Lagardere told French newspaper Le Figaro on Saturday he had been placed under investigation following a lawsuit brought in December 1992 by a shareholder for alleged fraud in the Matra Hachette buy out.
Luxury goods company LVMH rises 1.62 percent, helped by last week's announcement it plans to buy control of U.S. luxury goods distributor DFS.
Drugs firm Synthelabo up in active trading, up 3.48 percent. Traders say the stock is buoyed by now-familiar market talk of mergers in the sector.

Lens-maker Essilor was boosted 2.97 percent by hopes that glass-manufacturer Saint-Gobain may add to its stake in Essilor. Saint-Gobain chairman Jean-Louis Beffa told daily Le Figaro on Monday he did not rule out strengthenign ties and technology exchanges between the two companies.
Insurer UAP strengthens. Financial daily Les Echos had a round up of insurers' first-half results, which was viewed as positive for UAP, which was up 1.98 percent.
